title: `http_client` enhancement: pagination
bodyText:
(copied from #20844 )
I'm dealing with this one again with yet another API so I want to revive this discussion
I don't know what the correct general way to handle pagination is, since every API is going to be different. Okta handles it with a Link header, Kandji handles it with a next link in the payload, Slack handles it with response_metadata.next_cursor in the payload
I think that maybe one solution is to add a pagination section to the http_client source and allow the user to write VRL that will generate the next URL to fetch (or null to reset to whatever the original URL is?)
For something like the Okta streaming API (just as an example. I've written the Okta source to handle this specific case) the API always returns a rel=next link, and the client is meant to pause when the payload is empty but continue processing with that next link (or, in other words, the URL to process next cycle is updated rather than reset.) I suppose something like a reset_after_pagination option or some such?
The issues here I guess is how to expose a state machine to VRL (what indicates that it should stop?) and the internal configuration (ie, the url that it should hit next time)
I'm happy to actually make the change myself, and write an RFC around it but I'd like to hear from others first

title: SQS Source wrap up
bodyText:
Question
There are many questions related to the SQS source, and since I am currently investigating SQS, I figured it was worth consolidating them into a single summary question.
At the moment, we have several very busy SQS queues, with many billions of events per day. vector is handling this with ease (awesome work to everyone who's worked on the source/sink ❤️ )
Concurrency
The existing concurrency model has some room for improvement. When the SQS queue is very busy, all of the nodes' concurrency is running well, and we may see a slight increase in the max message age. However, when the message rate is slower, the number of consumers per host remains constant. This results in the CloudWatch metric NumberOfEmptyReceives increasing. When many nodes have a high concurrency level configured, this can result in unnecessary costs and wasted compute.
I've had a look at how this is handled in other sources or sinks, and there are several approaches. The current implementation of the SQS sink uses an adaptive concurrency model that appears to be based on round-trip time. A similar approach could be used to dynamically adjust the concurrency based on the message attribute SentTimestamp, which is already being extracted in get_timestamp().
A MessageAgeMonitor would need to be implemented to dynamically track and manage concurrency. The message age thresholds could be configured in the source, with a max concurrency value that defaults to the number of cores or a configured value. An alternative to strictly configured values is to use an exponentially weighted moving average of message ages. This is probably a more user-friendly approach, but it may need a broader discussion, as there are many possible approaches.
Another common approach across sinks is the common::backoff::ExponentialBackoff crate/module/library. Implementing this would be less work; however, I wanted to reach out to discuss and see what the maintainers prefer.
Message attributes
There are many different discussions and issues that cover this; it seems to be something that isn't outright rejected and is looking for someone to implement it. While I am sure that many people overload the use of attributes, one use case that is useful is encoding the source request_id or similar application metadata in the attributes and leaving the original message intact. Sometimes this is used for routing decisions because the message doesn't need to be deserialised or parsed.
Has anyone put any time into thinking about a preferred implementation for handling message attributes? My naive thinking has been to use the dropped_fields ObjectMap in the EventMetadata, but from reading issues and comments, that might not be the right choice.
SQS DLQ
SQS supports DLQ, in the scenario where receiving messages from external "untrusted" sources is possible, messages may not be well formed, or may have become corrupted (rare). Has there been any discussion about adding DLQ support for messages that can't be processed correctly the first x times?
These are items that we are in a position to resolve through sending in a PR, particularly the concurrency item as it's currently an item showing up in our aws bills. These would be submitted as separate smaller PR's based on whatever path forward can be agreed to (or not).
Thanks in advance,
James.

bodyText:
We have several use cases where we need to write events out as Avro- or Parquet-encoded data (e.g. to S3 and Kafka) so that downstream systems in our data platform can consume them directly.
Right now, the Avro support in Vector appears to be limited to using to_avro_datum. From the apache-avro docs:
NOTE: This function has a quite small niche of usage and does NOT generate headers and sync markers; use https://docs.rs/apache-avro/latest/apache_avro/struct.Writer.html to be fully Avro-compatible if you don’t know what you are doing, instead.

Because to_avro_datum only produces a single Avro-encoded value (no container file header, no sync markers, no codec metadata), the output isn’t directly compatible with the Avro Object Container File (OCF) format or with many “big data” tools that expect standard Avro files.
What we’d like to contribute
We’d like to improve Vector’s Avro compatibility so that it can:

Write fully compatible Avro object container files (OCF)

Use apache_avro::Writer (or an equivalent abstraction) so that:
The Avro file header is written, including:

avro.schema with the JSON schema
Sync markers are generated and written between blocks.


Target use case: writing Avro files to S3 / object storage that are consumable by Spark/Flink/other Avro tooling out of the box.
Keep the existing implementation so that it's not going to break existing users



Our goal is to make Vector’s Avro output “just work” with the broader Avro ecosystem (Java Avro, avro-tools, Spark, etc.), not only with custom consumers that know about the current to_avro_datum usage.
Proposed approach
If you’re open to this, we’d like to contribute this work as a series of small, incremental PRs that preserve existing behavior by default. Roughly:


Introduce an OCF writer path that uses apache_avro::Writer for file-style outputs, controlled via configuration (so the existing raw datum behavior can be kept for backward compatibility).


Add configuration options for:

datum (existing/default)
Avro Object Container (new)



Add compatibility tests, for example:

Golden Avro files produced by Vector that are validated with avro-tools / Java Avro.
Round-trip tests where data written by Vector is read back with the Rust apache-avro reader.



We’d really appreciate feedback on:

Whether you’d be willing to accept PRs in this direction.
Any existing design constraints we should be aware of (beyond the contributing guidelines, maybe this has been done before?).

title: Optimal way to access k8s labels having a sources type file
bodyText:
Question
Hello everyone!
I'm trying Vector as alternative for our current k8s log shipper pipeline (currently powered by Filebeat and Logstash).
I'm using the source type file instead of kubernetes_logs because I have a very heavy load on our cluster and I don't really want to stress the k8s API server to access logs, so I'm just reading them from this path /var/log/containers/*.log (at the moment as first PoC i've installed Vector as process running on a node with systemd, it's not a daemonset).
I'm getting almost everything just parsing the filename, for example:
/var/log/containers/grafana-f645ff4d7-2vqqv_minio_grafana-2455b25e0bf402fbf7cf7c5e202df3309ab4b24ae8b732ca74e4a2523bc3323f.log
I get grafana-f645ff4d7-2vqqv as pod name, minio as namespace and grafana as container name. The last part it's the container id.
Also I added a bunch of extra logic to get other fields, using some transforms type remap, which are out of scope for my post.
My question is, I have to add to my log a certain k8s Label called app.kubernetes.io/name: is it possible to get this information in some way? Like for example can I just read labels / metadata from my k8s without getting the whole log?
Of course I tried the source type kubernetes_logs (with that I indeed can access the label I want), but it adds too much overhead to be actually used in my production environment.

title: Q&A - Possible Socket (UDP) issue on 0.46.0+?
bodyText:
Question
Vector runs in K8S as our internal log ingestor/aggregator/normalizer, service is behind a metallb LoadBalancer IP. The normalized events are sent to Kafka and beyond after normalization.
We ran into an issue when ingesting events through Socket/UDP when we upgraded from 0.43.1 to 0.51.1.
On our current load, we had around ~15-17k events per second (Vector's internal metrics for received events on component_kind="source" and Kafka metrics for the sink's topic align on the numbers), after upgrading with the same config in place, we only see ~6-8k eps in both, so pretty much a 2x drop in both Vector & Kafka metrics. From some testing, we noticed that this issue appears starting with 0.46.0.
Extra info:

We looked at the container logs, enabled debug, but couldn't pin down any useful errors/traces to create an issue.
We tested a bunch of versions (starting with 0.45.0 up to 0.53.0), everything looks good on 0.45.0, then the "issue" starts on 0.46.0 and onwards.
We stripped the config down to just the sources and sinks (only metrics).
The containers typically never reach even ~50% resource usage

I've got some log_to_metric transforms happening, which feed to an aggregate.  This is a 1:1 flow - straight through, no many-to-one concentrations - super-simple. When I graph "vector_component_allocated_bytes" for all my components, I see the memory increasing (as expected) for the aggregation.  However, the log_to_metric that is feeing the aggregation is growing also, about three times larger! However... memory use on the log_to_metric doesn't go to zero, as I would expect.  It reduces to around half.  The aggregate drops only a small amount.

But the first interval just is skipped.  In fact, the aggregate CLIMBS sharply at the end of the first 6 hours, which is entirely counter-intuitive.

title: [Q&A] How to handle year boundary with parsing timestamp.
bodyText:
Question
Description
When parsing timestamps for logs that don't include year information, there's a problem with year extraction at year boundaries, causing log insertion failures.
is there a way to specify timezone when using now() or when parsing timestamps?
(without changing the timestamp format of the original log)
Log timestamp examples

ncdn: Nov  7 12:14:05.941 ...
dns: Jan  5 14:45:39

Problem

VictoriaLogs supports ISO8601/RFC3339 or unix timestamp formats
Therefore, Jan  5 14:45:39 needs to be converted to RFC3339 format with year information
At year boundaries, incorrect year values are extracted, causing log insertion failures

Root Cause

now() returns UTC time, but the actual logs are in KST (UTC+9)
During the period from 00:00 to 09:00 KST on January 1st, UTC time is still December 31st of the previous year
This causes the year to be set to the previous year, resulting in timestamps that are too old and failing VictoriaLogs retention period validation

Vector Config

.log_timestamp = to_string(.year) + " " + to_string!(.logdate) # When combining this way, during +09:00Z 2026/01/01 00:00 ~ 09:00, year value returns 2025, which converts to 2024 when converted +09:00Z.
.timestamp, err = parse_timestamp(.log_timestamp, format: "%Y %b %d %H:%M:%S")
